lore.summary: The spotlight offers fun, affordable or underappreciated games; hosts explicitly avoid hidden-gem hype and price-driving intent.

speaker.basis: Named Johnny/Kat opening and dialogue continuity; undiarized text, not audio-verified.

evidence.quote: we’re not really saying these are hidden gems
we’re not trying to make anything more expensive

lore.summary: Kat quotes cartridge-only Kickle Cubicle eBay prices of $12–20 and says local copies can be cheaper; dated anecdote, not current guidance.

speaker.basis: Named Johnny/Kat opening and dialogue continuity; undiarized text, not audio-verified.

evidence.quote: anywhere from $12 to $20
That’s card only
I have seen it locally cheaper

lore.summary: Kat presents Kickle Cubicle as a single-player puzzle game with magic-bag collection, lands, bosses and ice-block attacks; mechanics are reported, not independently verified.

speaker.basis: Named Johnny/Kat opening and dialogue continuity; undiarized text, not audio-verified.

evidence.quote: It’s a single player
collect all of these magic bags
throw little ice blocks

lore.summary: Kat dislikes the Tetris/Dr. Mario style and finds Kickle Cubicle a different, increasingly difficult but enjoyable alternative.

speaker.basis: Named Johnny/Kat opening and dialogue continuity; undiarized text, not audio-verified.

evidence.quote: I’m really not a Tetris fan
It does get, I find, quite hard

lore.summary: Johnny says he reads Dr. Mario horizontally, struggles, and is teased while playing by his wife and a friend. This is contextual attribution, not a medical/ability diagnosis.

speaker.basis: Named Johnny/Kat opening and dialogue continuity; undiarized text, not audio-verified.

evidence.quote: I look at it left to right instead of up and down
my wife and one of my good friends
I feel like if I turn the screen sideways

lore.summary: Kat's strongest comparison is Chip’s Challenge; Lolo comparison stays tentative because she has played only some of it.

speaker.basis: Named Johnny/Kat opening and dialogue continuity; undiarized text, not audio-verified.

evidence.quote: loosely of Chip’s Challenge
I’ve played Lolo some
I don’t know how much I would say it’s the same

lore.summary: Kat discovered Kickle Cubicle's animated vegetables after trying it, and the hosts joke about an A for animated vegetables.

speaker.basis: Named Johnny/Kat opening and dialogue continuity; undiarized text, not audio-verified.

evidence.quote: Actually, I found out after
A for animated vegetables

lore.summary: Johnny's pre-release remake concerns concern non-turn-based combat, visual style and episodic structure; he allows that it could still turn out well.

speaker.basis: Named Johnny/Kat opening and dialogue continuity; undiarized text, not audio-verified.

evidence.quote: maybe, maybe it’ll be great
I don’t like the lack of turn-based combat. I don’t like the visual look. I don’t like it being broken into episodes

lore.summary: Johnny reports buying a PlayStation for the original Final Fantasy VII and owning about five versions of that game; this is not a remake purchase.

speaker.basis: Named Johnny/Kat opening and dialogue continuity; undiarized text, not audio-verified.

evidence.quote: This the game I bought a PlayStation for
I own like five versions of Final Fantasy seven

lore.summary: Johnny supplies VI/US III and IV/US II regional-numbering explanations; the episode explicitly connects these labels, unlike unrelated similarly numbered games.

speaker.basis: Named Johnny/Kat opening and dialogue continuity; undiarized text, not audio-verified.

evidence.quote: six is the Japanese numbering. Three is what it was here in America on the Super Nintendo
Final Fantasy two or four in Japan

lore.summary: Johnny calls Final Fantasy IV a favorite but disliked the episodic After Years additions, offered as a cautionary comparison.

speaker.basis: Named Johnny/Kat opening and dialogue continuity; undiarized text, not audio-verified.

evidence.quote: Final Fantasy four is one of my favorite games
I hated playing episodic, like extra additions

lore.summary: Quarterly-report timing, publisher cash motives, microtransactions, part counts and prices are speculative possibilities in 2015, not established plans.

speaker.basis: Named Johnny/Kat opening and dialogue continuity; undiarized text, not audio-verified.

evidence.quote: Maybe they’ve got bad quarterly reports coming
Maybe three
Are we like looking at like $15 per episode

lore.summary: The hosts read an attributed Square Enix statement about multiple entries and full-sized content. The attribution is preserved without independently verifying the original press statement.

speaker.basis: Named Johnny/Kat opening and dialogue continuity; undiarized text, not audio-verified.

evidence.quote: Square Enix updated a reply
each entry will have the volume of content equal to a full-sized game

lore.summary: Johnny recalls extensive original Final Fantasy VII play after a breakup around age 18, with jokingly hedged 100-hour talk; exact duration and private biography are not established.

speaker.basis: Named Johnny/Kat opening and dialogue continuity; undiarized text, not audio-verified.

evidence.quote: Some of us may have done that
I may have just broken up with a girlfriend

lore.summary: Johnny dislikes the Advent Children-style realism for Cloud and the oversized sword, but calls it a personal quibble.

speaker.basis: Named Johnny/Kat opening and dialogue continuity; undiarized text, not audio-verified.

evidence.quote: Advent Children format
the more real it looks, the more impractical the sword looks

lore.summary: Long materia/summon animations prompt a make-a-sandwich joke; Knights of the Round is a spell/summon context, not a separate game review.

lore.summary: Johnny intends to play at least the remake's first episode and avoid reviews; Kat wants a later opinion check. No actual remake gameplay, purchase or follow-up result occurs here.

evidence.quote: I’m gonna play the first episode at least
I’m going to try not read reviews

lore.summary: Johnny strongly dislikes VIII, is okay with IX, and reports getting through most of XII before rejecting it; this is his taste, not universal agreement.
